readings.title: Eliphaz's Third Speech
readings.subtitle: Accusations of Great Evil
readings.text: [Job 22:1] And Eliphaz the Těmanite answered and said, [2] “Would a strong man be of use to <dn>Ěl</dn>? Even he who is wise be of use to <dn>Him</dn>? [3] Is it a delight to the <dn>Almighty</dn> that you are righteous? Or gain, that you make your ways perfect? [4] Is it because of your fear of <dn>Him</dn> that <dn>He</dn> reproves you, or enters into right-ruling with you? [5] Is not your evil great? And is there no end to your crookednesses? [6] For you take pledges from your brother for naught, and strip the naked of their garments. [7] You do not give the weary water to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry. [8] But the man of strength, he has the earth, and the highly respected man dwells in it. [9] You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless are crushed. [10] Therefore snares are all around you, and sudden fear alarms you, [11] or darkness, so that you do not see, and a flood of water covers you. [12] Is not <dn>Eloah</dn> in the height of heaven? And see the highest stars, how lofty they are! [13] And you have said, ‘What does <dn>Ěl</dn> know? Would <dn>He</dn> judge through the dark cloud? [14] Clouds screen <dn>Him</dn>, so that <dn>He</dn> does not see, and <dn>He</dn> moves about the circuit of the heavens.’ [15] Do you observe the old way which wicked men have trod, [16] who were cut down before their time, whose foundations were swept away by a flood? [17] They said to <dn>Ěl</dn>, ‘Turn aside from us!’ And what did the <dn>Almighty</dn> do to them? [18] Yet <dn>He</dn> filled their houses with the good! (But the counsel of the wrong has been far from me). [19] The righteous see it and are glad, and the innocent mock at them and say, [20] Truly, our adversaries are cut off, and fire has consumed their excess.’ [21] Be of service to <dn>Him</dn>, and be at peace; thereby blessing shall come to you. [22] Please accept the Torah from <dn>His</dn> mouth, and lay up <dn>His</dn> words in your heart. [23] If you return to the <dn>Almighty</dn>, you are built up. If you remove unrighteousness far from your tents, [24] and lay your gold in the dust, and the gold of Ophir among the stones of the wadis, [25] then the <dn>Almighty</dn> shall be your gold and your silver, strength to you. [26] Then you shall certainly delight in the <dn>Almighty</dn>, and lift up your face to <dn>Eloah</dn>, [27] make your prayer to <dn>Him</dn>. And <dn>He</dn> shall hear you, and you shall pay your vows. [28] And whatever you decide on shall be established for you, and light shine on your ways. [29] For they have made low, and you say, ‘Up!’ And <dn>He</dn> saves the lowly of eyes. [30] Would <dn>He</dn> deliver one who is not innocent? So by the cleanness of your hands you shall be delivered.”

readings.title: Iyoḇ's Reply to Eliphaz
readings.subtitle: Longing for the Almighty's Presence
readings.text: [Job 23:1] And Iyoḇ answered and said, [2] “Even today my complaint is bitter; my hand is heavy on account of my groaning. [3] If only I knew where to find <dn>Him</dn>, I would come to <dn>His</dn> dwelling-place! [4] I would present my case before <dn>Him</dn>, and fill my mouth with proofs. [5] I would know the words which <dn>He</dn> would answer me, and understand what <dn>He</dn> would say to me. [6] Would <dn>He</dn> contend with me in great power? No! But <dn>He</dn> would pay attention to me. [7] There the upright might reason with <dn>Him</dn>, and I would go safe forever from my Judge. [8] See, I go forward, but <dn>He</dn> is not; and backward, but I do not perceive <dn>Him</dn>; [9] to the left where <dn>He</dn> is working, but I do not see; <dn>He</dn> turns to the right, but I do not see. [10] For <dn>He</dn> knows the way that I take. When <dn>He</dn> has tried me, I would come forth as gold. [11] My foot has held fast to <dn>His</dn> steps. I have guarded <dn>His</dn> way, and did not turn aside. [12] I have not strayed from the command of <dn>His</dn> lips. I have treasured the words of <dn>His</dn> mouth more than my own law. [13] But <dn>He</dn> is One, and who does turn <dn>Him</dn>? And <dn>He</dn> does whatever <dn>His</dn> being has desired. [14] For <dn>He</dn> makes complete my law, and many like these are with <dn>Him</dn>. [15] Therefore I am troubled at <dn>His</dn> presence; I consider, and I am afraid of <dn>Him</dn>. [16] For <dn>Ěl</dn> has made me faint-hearted, and the <dn>Almighty</dn> has alarmed me; [17] because I was not cut off before darkness, and from my face <dn>He</dn> has covered the thick darkness.

readings.title: Iyoḇ's Complaint of Injustice
readings.subtitle: The Wicked Go Unpunished
readings.text: [Job 24:1] “Times are not hidden from the <dn>Almighty</dn>, and why have not those who know <dn>Him</dn> seen <dn>His</dn> days? [2] They remove landmarks; they rob and feed on flocks; [3] they drive away the donkey of the fatherless; they take the widow’s ox as a pledge; [4] they turn the needy out of the way; the poor of the earth have hidden together. [5] See, as wild donkeys in the wilderness they go about their tasks, eager seekers for prey; the desert gives his bread, for the children. [6] They reap his fodder in a field and they glean the vineyard of the wrong. [7] They spend the night naked, without a garment, and without covering in the cold. [8] They are wet with the showers of the hills, and have embraced a rock for lack of shelter. [9] They snatch away the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge from the poor; [10] naked, they shall go about without a garment; and hungry, they shall take away sheaves. [11] They press out oil within their walls; winepresses they shall tread, yet suffer thirst. [12] Men groan in the city, and the beings of the wounded cry out, and <dn>Eloah</dn> does not regard it as foolish. [13] They have become rebels against the light; they have not known <dn>His</dn> ways nor remained in <dn>His</dn> paths. [14] The murderer rises at daylight, he kills· the poor and needy, and in the night he is as a thief. [15] And the eye of the adulterer watches for dusk, saying, ‘No eye sees me.’ And he puts a covering on the face. [16] In the dark he has broken into houses; by day they shut themselves up; they have not known light. [17] For all of them morning is the same as the shadow of death, when he discerns the extreme fears of the shadow of death. [18] He is swift on the face of the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth; he does not turn into the way of vineyards. [19] Drought and heat snatch away snow waters – She’ol those who have sinned. [20] The womb forgets him, the worm feeds sweetly on him; he is remembered no more, and wickedness is broken like a tree; [21] treating evil the barren who does not bear, and does no good for the widow. [22] But <dn>He</dn> draws the mighty away with <dn>His</dn> power – <dn>He</dn> rises up, and no one is certain of life. [23] <dn>He</dn> gives him safety, and he leans on it; yet <dn>His</dn> eyes are on their ways. [24] They are lifted up for a little while, then they are gone, then they shall be brought low. Like all else they are gathered up, and they are cut off like the heads of grain. [25] And if it is not so, who does prove me a liar, and make my word worthless?”

readings.title: Bildaḏ's Third Speech
readings.subtitle: The Majesty of Ěl
readings.text: [Job 25:1] And Bildaḏ the Shuḥite answered and said, [2] “Rule and fear belong to <dn>Him</dn>, making peace in <dn>His</dn> high places. [3] Is there any number to <dn>His</dn> armies? And on whom does <dn>His</dn> light not rise? [4] So how could man be righteous before <dn>Ěl</dn>? Or how could he be flawless who is born of a woman? [5] See, even the moon does not shine, and the stars have not been flawless in <dn>His</dn> eyes, [6] how much less man, a maggot, and a son of man, a worm?”
